items.gist: Siddhi is nonconceptual consciousness of the thing, not something produced by vikalpa.
Consciousness gathers distinctions even in darkness; purity of consciousness is discussed and fivefold samāveśa is introduced.
The tattvas and puṃvidyāśakti pervade; distinctions arise by purity and impurity.
Elements are established by inference and pervade the fourfold states.
Fivefold rudraśakti samāveśa is discussed; the nondual mahādevī differs from dualist tattvas.
The world-form of earth and others is treated; parts lead to partless insight.
Śiva is worshipped through qualities; devotees rest in the full dharmi.
The nonconceptual self is not made an object; subtle luminous consciousness is described.
Qualities are śaktis; anantā and mitā śaktis imply bhairava and other levels.
The nonconceptual path leads to Śiva through any path up to earth.
The conceptual path works through māyā; the paśu's avikalpā bhūmi and contraction are explained.
Conceptual certainty defines the āṇava upāya, which lacks uccāra distinctions.
Śiva himself pervades as buddhi and manas; dualist texts are cited in support.
Both samāveśas lead to the nonconceptual ocean; conceptual validity is subordinate.
Ratna tattva is mentioned; śāmbhava, śākta, and āṇava upāyas are distinguished.
All action is knowledge in sequence, dependent on the upāya.
Right knowledge is the sole cause of liberation; the guru's continuum liberates.
An objection asks how dīkṣā can liberate if knowledge alone does.
Mala is like an eye-film; dīkṣā removes it, and further refutation follows.
